direction: Research is guidance; only curated paintings and verified predicates become runtime scenes.

regions.label: Elwynn Forest and Stormwind Hinterland
regions.facts: Broad old hardwood trunks, rounded green crowns, clear brooks, meadow glades and cultivated valleys create an intimate, fertile woodland heartland. Human timber-and-plaster farms and blue-roofed stonework supply the inherited regional building vocabulary; new fittings follow the current inhabitants. Canals and dense urban masonry belong to actual built districts, while rural scenes keep the forest close.

regions.label: Westfall
regions.facts: Open rolling agricultural country, long sightlines, coastal wind, golden grain or dry grass, timber windmills, field walls, stone-and-timber farmsteads, weathered barns, sandy beaches and low rocky bluffs. Keep its wind-driven working landscape and big skies. Failed harvests, abandoned buildings, drought and bandit occupation are current conditions rather than compulsory consequences of the region name.

regions.label: Brightwood / Duskwood
regions.facts: The same southern woodland can appear as living Brightwood or curse-darkened Duskwood. Maintain dense mature trees, damp hollows, old field boundaries and small timber-and-plaster settlements. Under an established shadow curse, branches knot and thin, blue-green gloom and low mist replace daylight, and warm lantern pools become socially important. Cemeteries, watch posts and burial architecture are site-specific facilities.

regions.label: Redridge Mountains
regions.facts: Warm ochre and rusty foothills, elm and pine woodland, autumn-colored crowns, rocky gullies and clear inland waters. Steep ridges overlook fertile pockets and small lake settlements. Grey bridge masonry, timber buildings, red roofs, sawmill materials and practical defensive stations supply inherited local craft. The region is temperate and traversable, distinct from the volcanic country immediately north.

regions.label: Burning Steppes
regions.facts: A volcanic highland of blackened slopes, ash-colored ground, heat-reddened sky, jagged spurs, charred timber and scattered older stonework. This destruction predates the usual GoA2 campaigns; ordinary scenes retain its geology while current lava activity, war damage and industrial occupation follow local state. Forge camps and supply yards can support travelers or temporary government without recreating Blackrock's famous silhouette.

regions.label: Deadwind Pass
regions.facts: A narrow southern Redridge corridor of steep grey rock, ravines, constrained crossings and old habitation. Living woodland and clear water are possible before the established magical devastation; the familiar haunted state uses skeletal trees, grey-blue sky, lifeless ground and thin cold haze. Show ordinary pass structures and remnants, leaving Karazhan and its distinctive tower composition to the iconic-location pass.

regions.label: Swamp of Sorrows
regions.facts: Warm olive-green bayous, spreading trees, hanging moss, shallow brown-green water, reed banks and broken raised ground. Timber causeways, stilt platforms, boat slips and roofs lifted above damp stores are its practical regional language. Older troll masonry can survive as a site feature; existing settlements adopt local cultural ornament while retaining the requirements of the swamp.

regions.label: Black Morass / Blasted Lands
regions.facts: The southern Black Morass is a physical-state pair: dark wetland, low hills and woodland before devastation; burnt rust-red earth, broken rock, sparse dead growth and an unnatural purple-grey sky after portal-related damage. Keep geography and existing routes stable while the terrain treatment changes. The Dark Portal itself is reserved for an iconic scene; a ruler's ancestry or faith cannot establish this landscape transformation.

regions.label: Northern Stranglethorn
regions.facts: Steaming jungle, massive roots and vines, steep river banks, bright tropical foliage and warm filtered light. Ancient Gurubashi cut stone, stepped platforms and carved animal faces remain part of the landscape where ruins exist. Timber bridges, hunting shelters and extraction yards serve movement through difficult vegetation. Political owners and current enterprises supply movable ornament and active uses.

regions.label: Cape of Stranglethorn
regions.facts: Tropical coasts, palm-fringed cliffs, sheltered coves, salt-weathered timber, boats, rope bridges and stacked trading buildings. The sea connects the jungle to a cosmopolitan shipping economy. Generic harbors and beach stopping places share this vocabulary; Booty Bay's exact shape, statue and distinctive waterfront composition remain for the iconic-location pass.

regions.label: Dun Morogh
regions.facts: Snowy mountain valleys, tall dark conifers, blue-white rock, clear cold air, stone roads and heavy masonry fitted to steep terrain. Sturdy lodges, supply halls and mining yards link travel to warmth, craft and mountain logistics. Gnomish mechanical chambers are restricted to actual engineered settlements and underground works; they do not turn every snowfield into Gnomeregan.

regions.label: Badlands
regions.facts: Red-orange mesas, cracked ochre earth, deep dry canyons, sparse thorny scrub and great exposed fossil remains. Rock shelters, expedition yards, mine entries and retained ancient cut stone fit this harsh interior. Later Cataclysm fissures and the occupation of any particular faction are separate states; ordinary scenes preserve the dramatic dry-land geology and the material importance of shade and water.

regions.label: Searing Gorge
regions.facts: A harsh volcanic gorge with steep cut chasms, grey-red dust, dark fissured rock, metal gantries, chains, timber supports and strongly worked industrial terraces. Where mines operate, the landscape joins immense excavation to masterwork smithing. The use and condition of each installation follow current occupation, while the gorge and its volcanic legacy remain the regional foundation.

regions.label: Wetlands
regions.facts: A broad lowland delta of shallow channels, reed beds, wet grass, spreading trees and mist under a steep mountain rim. Raised roads, bridges, timber landings, sturdy storehouses and coastal shipping join upland routes to the sea. Pre-Cataclysm dry port districts and later flooded streets are separate treatments; ordinary scenes favor working marsh access rather than a universal ruined harbor.

regions.label: Loch Modan
regions.facts: A temperate inland lake basin below high mountain shoulders: green pasture, tall pines, grey rocky shores and durable worked stone. Bridges, lakeside lodges, stone roads, hunting shelters and practical shore landings connect settlements and craft to freshwater. The intact lake is the principal baseline; a drained bed and broken hydraulic works require actual destruction or altered water levels.

regions.label: Northeron uplands
regions.facts: For GoA2’s pre-Cataclysm Northeron, commit to a storm-lashed Wildhammer mountain homeland: ominous high peaks, snow and ice at altitude, dense ironwood forest, greener valleys and rugged coasts, deep stone shelters and powerful cliffside flying-mount yards where those facilities exist. Combine the lore’s frozen mountain storms with inspected neighboring highland pine-and-rock forms. Separate this historical landscape from later catastrophic wreckage. Local cultural identity and active mount facilities still need present-campaign support.

regions.label: The Far Highlands
regions.facts: Northeastern Khaz Modan highland country beyond the inland lochs: imposing ridges, green forest pockets, river-cut ravines and a rugged coast. Separate intact highland grass-and-wood country from genuinely petrified obsidian woodland, dead terrain or elemental fractures. Present cultural overlays can be Wildhammer, Dragonmaw, draconic or newly hybrid without replacing the underlying geography. Black glass and mineral veins persist as physical materials where present; active purple corruption and floating rocks require specific campaign state.

regions.label: Arathi Highlands
regions.facts: Wide grassy uplands, broad-leaved isolated trees, scattered pines and rocky ridges, with strong road lines and old imperial stonework. A more open, exposed landscape than the neighboring forests: wind, changing cloud light, green-gold grasses and defended road junctions. Human Arathorian ruins or maintained foundations can persist beneath new occupants. Ordinary farm terraces, quarry yards and modest forts supply social use without reproducing Stromgarde or an iconic battleground.

regions.label: Hillsbrad Foothills
regions.facts: Rain-fed, fertile rolling farmland with green meadows, scattered pines, cultivated tracts, rivers, farm tracks and a gentle, windy southern seaboard. Northern views rise toward Alterac; healthy agricultural abundance distinguishes Hillsbrad from corrupted neighboring wealds. Human rural masonry, broad yards, barns and mills establish the inherited settlement fabric. Current occupants and later destruction must be separate overlays.

regions.label: Dalaran lake country and lesser arcane quarters
regions.facts: Cool, damp southern Lordamere lake country beneath Alterac’s rise, with cultivated approaches and a strong inherited arcane civic architecture. Pale carved masonry, violet tiled roofs, curving gold-toned trim, slender arches, manicured greenery and blue crystal lights distinguish maintained mage-built quarters. Ordinary visitor arcades, study courtyards and lake landings can carry this style without depicting the Violet Citadel or the city’s unique skyline. Destruction, a protective dome, relocation and a crater are separate campaign states.

regions.label: Alterac Mountains
regions.facts: A steep central Lordaeron mountain range with pine-covered lower slopes, gray crags, cold mist and a sharp transition toward snowbound uplands. Roads thread narrow passes; ruined or intact human stone towers, mining works and rare fertile valleys give travel social purpose. Snow belongs to elevation and season, rather than every foothill. Maintain the proud mountain-kingdom fabric where preserved, and separately gate destruction or hostile occupation.

regions.label: Gilneas
regions.facts: A cold maritime peninsula of frequent rain, gray cliffs, river valleys, moors, dense pines, dark broad-leaved woodland and rugged mountains. Its inherited architecture has sharply pitched slate roofs, tall chimneys, heavy dark timber, gray stone, iron railings and restrained manor-house formality. Warm enclosed interiors contrast with wet outdoor travel. Worgen, invasion, quarantine walls, flooding and abandonment remain campaign conditions rather than default inhabitants or events.

regions.label: Silverpine Forest
regions.facts: An immense coastal conifer forest: towering slender silver-barked pines, moist needle beds, mossy rock overhangs, small green hills and ground mist. Interior paths feel enclosed; western coasts are rugged, eastern waters belong to the lake country. Rural stone-and-timber houses and mills can exist intact. Southern villages may carry Gilnean steep-roofed, chimney-rich architecture. Cold gray-green light and occasional warm windows make shelter matter.

regions.label: Tirisfal Glades
regions.facts: Damp, rolling Lordaeron countryside with dense conifers, broad dark trees, mossy timber crossings, mills, cultivated clearings and old human masonry. Low mist and filtered light give the glades depth. Tirisfal retains the infrastructure of a wealthy agrarian heartland. When actually plagued, shift foliage toward purple-black, introduce green-yellow diseased sap and deteriorated farms; its signature is infected woodland, rather than making every tree an enormous mushroom.

regions.label: Western Weald / Western Plaguelands
regions.facts: The western Lordaeron weald is a former grain-rich agricultural belt: substantial farms, granaries, wooded roads, lake margins and older civic stonework. Healthy or reclaimed stretches use fertile greens and thriving crops. Active plague replaces these with rust-orange haze, diseased trees or giant spotted mushrooms, ruined farmyards and unsafe ground. The agricultural infrastructure remains its central identity in either state; it must not simply duplicate the more devastated Eastweald.

regions.label: Eastweald / Eastern Plaguelands
regions.facts: A wooded eastern Lordaeron interior of rising northern terrain, farming villages, mills, old roads and southern lake country. The famed plague-era look is extremely distinctive: dead brown earth, orange atmospheric haze, towering speckled mushrooms, skeletal trees and shattered settlement fabric. Build a separate healthy Eastweald state rather than carrying late canonical destruction into every campaign. Watchtowers and road shelters are reusable infrastructure, with ownership determined dynamically.

regions.label: The Hinterlands
regions.facts: Dense green conifer woodland enclosed by imposing reddish-gray mountain walls, open grass clearings, scattered lakes and a rugged eastern coast. Steep approaches support cliffside dwellings and gryphon infrastructure; low forest clearings support timber settlements and older troll stonework. Wildhammer, high-elven and forest-troll architecture are conditional cultural layers on a strong shared woodland landscape. Keep ancient ruins and sacred trees ordinary rather than reproducing named sites.

regions.label: Tol Barad
regions.facts: Cold maritime island; rain-dark masonry, low rough grass, dead or wind-stunted trees, grey sea, rusted iron, guarded supply routes and weather-beaten farms. Fortifications are enduring material; active imprisonment, ghosts, military occupation and damage follow the actual save.

regions.label: Channel Islands
regions.facts: A temperate naval archipelago: wooded ridges, brown sand or shingle coves, rocky channels, pasture pockets and modest coastal masonry. GoA2 groups Crestfall, Tol Ronal, Tol Dagor, Frostsabre and Havenswood here; exact island subtypes can override the shared base.

regions.label: Darkmoon Island
regions.facts: Murky violet maritime light, tangled dark woodland, crooked branches, damp paths and shadowed rocky beaches. Brilliant purple, green and gold showmanship appears only in a verified active or maintained fairground; the island is not necessarily hosting a fair during every visit.

regions.label: Zul'Dare
regions.facts: Temperate wooded naval island with concealed coves, freshwater clearings and defended approaches. Orc or Kul Tiran buildings are occupancy overlays. The troll-like name does not establish a jungle-troll homeland.

regions.label: Isle of Quel’Danas
regions.facts: A luminous northern island with pale sandy shore, cool green-blue water, golden-leaved trees, green coastal grass and graceful pale-stone elven structures. Maritime landings, garden shelters and ordinary store courts support visitors and travel while sacred importance can be conveyed by disciplined maintenance and refined craft. The Sunwell and famous terrace are reserved for iconic scenes. Demonic occupation, holy restoration and battle damage require actual campaign state.

regions.label: Eversong Woods
regions.facts: Radiant gold and amber canopy over healthy green ground, twisting pale trunks, clear streams, red-gold or blue-silver elven architectural forms and elegant roads. The golden leaves coexist with enchanted spring: describe magic-sustained freshness, not ordinary autumn decay. Runestones, floating devices and magical lamps require maintained arcane infrastructure. Regional inherited architecture survives political changes; current culture and faith control new symbols, reception customs and living occupants.

regions.label: Southern Eversong / Ghostlands
regions.facts: Southern Quel’Thalas shares the older woodland, river and elven settlement fabric of Eversong, with Amani border forest near its eastern reaches. The Ghostlands state strips away sustained spring: bare bleached branches, cold blue-black ground, lingering green corruption, damaged pavilions and empty woodland settlements. Healthy early-era southern Eversong can use golden woodland infrastructure. Retained damage does not require current Scourge ownership, and restoration must remove corresponding ruin/corruption assumptions.

regions.label: Zul’Aman and Amani forestlands
regions.facts: A temperate, shadowed conifer forest of immense trees, hilly borders, rivers and ancient Amani stonework. Forest settlements use strong timber platforms, carved posts, woven materials and animal imagery; monumental stepped masonry appears as an inherited regional layer in ordinary smaller fragments. Masks, drums, woodcarving and guarded communal space give active local settlements social form where culture supports them. Ruins need not imply abandonment of the surrounding civilization.

regions.label: Tiragarde Sound
regions.facts: Cool green maritime country around sheltered sounds: grey crags, conifers, upland snow, rough coves, shipbuilding timber, heavy piers, copper-green roofs and nautical machinery. Ports, wooded hunting country and highland routes coexist; pirate or cartel control is a current institution, not scenery everywhere.

regions.label: Drustvar
regions.facts: Rugged forested mountains; rust-red autumn foliage, dark gnarled trees, cold blue shadow, steep stone-roofed settlements, mines, hunting lodges and ancient Drust stonework. Folkloric menace is environmental; active witchcraft, wicker constructs or a corrupted tree require matching state.

regions.label: Stormsong Valley
regions.facts: Rich green rolling country, stone-edged fields, flowers, streams, windmills and grazing ground under rounded mountain walls; tidal coasts and shipbuilding facilities at the edges. Tide-sage religious fittings, void corruption and specific houses are independent overlays.

regions.label: Mechagon
regions.facts: Small rocky island with remnant conifer woods, dusty tracks and spectacular machine detritus; rusty gears, exposed piping, bright technical indicators and underground engineered access. Mechanical civilization is established material; king, rebellion, forced augmentation and hostile machines are historical/current state.

regions.label: Ashenvale
regions.facts: An ancient, living northern Kalimdor forest: immense trunks and spreading roots, dark emerald canopy, purple and blue undergrowth, clear woodland waters, moss-softened pale stone and scattered pre-Sundering elven masonry. Routes feel threaded through an older world rather than carved across an ordinary European wood. Logging, military occupation and fel damage are local overlays selected from current state.

regions.label: Moonglade
regions.facts: A deep green, mountain-sheltered woodland basin focused on a clear lake, with enormous old trees, long soft twilight, roots, ferns and restrained crafted shelters. Druidic assembly and sanctuary are important native site uses when their institutions remain active. A change in control need not erase physical woodland and old craft, but sanctuary law is selected from current authority.

regions.label: Darkshore
regions.facts: A narrow, shadowed evergreen coast pressed between western sea and mountain wall: grey beaches, dark rock, low sea mist, kelp, river mouths and ancient elven remains. Coastal work and sea passage are central. Storm and fog vary with weather; Cataclysm fractures, burnt woods and warfront works require matching events and are not the baseline.

regions.label: Pinkwood / Felwood when corrupted
regions.facts: A long forested mountain approach with old woodland, streams, ravines and ancient remnants. Before established demonic corruption it belongs to the lush Ashenvale forest vocabulary. Fel corruption transforms living timber and water into sickly green, scarred, foul terrain; recovery appears in patches and maintained enclaves. Select an actual landscape state before choosing the block.

regions.label: Azshara
regions.facts: Eternal autumn on a fractured coast: red and orange trees, golden grasses, pale carved elven ruins, dramatic cliffs, sandy coves and glimpses of blue sea. Ancient imperial remains give the region grandeur even in small scenes. Goblin highways, industrial cuttings, enormous machines and a faction-shaped coast require current construction or associated state; avoid making Cataclysm development timeless.

regions.label: Mount Hyjal
regions.facts: A vast, ancient mountain landscape: steep wooded ascents, grey ridges, giant roots, pine forest, watercourses and high sheltered terraces. Sacred woodland grandeur is physical even under changing rulers. World Tree infrastructure requires the local root system; burned battlefields, active lava and elemental siege are separate state variants, not a permanent mountain-wide default.

regions.label: Winterspring
regions.facts: A high, permanently snowy northern valley: white and lavender drifts, firs, hard blue shadows, pale rocky slopes, clear cold air and pockets of geothermal steam. Frostsaber hunting, fur and supplies fit local travel but no beast or faction is mandatory. Goblin commerce is an established cultural settlement option, not the whole regional landscape.

regions.label: Kalidar / conditional Teldrassil
regions.facts: Before the World Tree, use a forested northern island: sheltering groves, rocky shores, sea approaches and small settlements shaped by current inhabitants. After actual growth of Teldrassil, add immense living boughs, elevated forest ground, violet and silver woodland, branch-built circulation and magical means of ascent where supported. Neither Darnassus nor a giant living Tree is an automatic feature of the regional label.

regions.label: Durotar
regions.facts: Durotar is cracked red earth and orange rock, with dry ravines, sheer eroded shoulders, sparse tough scrub and the bright sea close beside the harsh interior. Use bold Warcraft rock silhouettes and a red-dust coating on working objects. Timber, hide, rough cordage and heavy practical metal suit existing frontier settlements; choose their cultural forms through the current settlement layer. Shade and fresh water are valuable spatial resources. The region must remain recognizable after its rulers, faith and builders change.

regions.label: Echo Isles
regions.facts: These islands are a tropical maritime counterpoint to mainland Durotar: pale sand, warm shallows, palm shade, dense pockets of greenery and many short stretches of water between settlement spaces. Island travel uses boats, raised timber landings and narrow bridges where those have been built. Local Darkspear craft supplies strong examples of thatch, lashed timber, tusk-shaped supports, vivid bindings and painted carvings; apply those details when its builders remain present. Boat care, fishing, provisions and shared shaded gathering are the reusable regional functions.

regions.label: The Barrens
regions.facts: The Barrens is enormous exposed savanna rather than uniform desert: straw-gold grasses, rust-brown soil, flat-topped acacia-like trees, scattered rocky hills and long routes between water sources. Broad visibility and scarce shade distinguish it from Durotar ravines. Waterholes make greener, denser pockets; the eastern shore supports ordinary maritime trade. Southern thorn country needs giant coiling razor-brambles as a physical terrain overlay, not generic woodland. Routes, animal handling and cargo handling should visibly require space. Do not insert the Cataclysm lava division into the baseline.

regions.label: Dustwallow Marsh
regions.facts: Dustwallow is a warm, ancient swamp of dark channels, waterlogged earth and huge moss-draped trees. The palette is subdued brown, olive and gray-green with warmer lantern light. Raised roads, bridges, piles and dry storage make ordinary life feasible; the coast offers firmer maritime settlement space. Fishing, boat maintenance and moving supplies matter more than scenic gardens. Human, ogre, troll, goblin or other current settlements overlay their forms onto the same wet environment. A ruined inn, Theramore destruction or a dragon attack belongs to a site or actual state, not the default region.

regions.label: Mulgore
regions.facts: Mulgore is green rolling pasture enclosed by mountains, with pine groves, clear water and immense flat-topped mesas. Its regional palette is fresh grass-green and gold, cool blue distance and warm hide-and-timber settlements when tauren construction remains. Large animals and inhabitants require broad approaches, plentiful room around shelters and practical stock management. Height supplies observation and gathering places above the grazing plain. Keep ordinary mesa settlements and smaller camps distinct from iconic Thunder Bluff itself; current culture supplies household ornament and authority signs.

regions.label: Stonetalon Mountains
regions.facts: Red sandstone mountains and deeply cut canyons alternate with cool pine valleys, lakes and wooded heights. Routes are constrained by ravines and cliff openings. Forestry and mining fit the terrain when an operation exists, with timber, carts and machinery added as worksite layers. Charred or magically scorched valleys and later military devastation are localized state variants.

regions.label: Feralas
regions.facts: Feralas is immense humid old-growth forest: deep greens, giant trunks, dangling vines, moss and mist, with rivers and wet fern-heavy ground. Weathered elven stone can survive as physical ruins wherever mapped, while working settlements reflect their actual builders. Its shore and nearby islands share the dense forest meeting pale sand and ocean. The forest conceals approaches, but maintained clearings and river landings make usable social spaces. Keep ancient ruin fragments ordinary and dispersed; Dire Maul and Feathermoon are reserved for the later iconic-location pass.

regions.label: Desolace
regions.facts: The baseline interior is bone-gray, dusty and rocky, with immense weathered hills, sparse dead-looking trees and bleached kodo remains. It is distinct from the warm savanna and golden Tanaris dunes. Surviving water and the greener western coastal shelves are strong contrasts. Centaur hide-and-timber camps are useful construction references when present, with wide body access and practical corrals. Do not encode the canonical centaur wars as a current event, or the Cataclysm restoration as universal greenery. Restoration scenes require an actually changed physical landscape.

regions.label: Thousand Needles and the Shimmering Flats
regions.facts: The dry baseline is a deep orange-red canyon crowded with slender rock pillars and larger flat-topped mesas. Height, narrow routes and carefully built connections dominate settlement access; rope bridges and lifts are physical infrastructure rather than guaranteed objects. The eastern Shimmering Flats is an intensely pale open salt pan, requiring its own flatter imagery. The later canonical flooding is a separate landscape state. A flooded scene should show the same surviving columns rising from water and boat access replacing the old canyon floor, only when the active map or simulation actually supports that state.

regions.label: Uldum riverlands and desert
regions.facts: Uldum is a sharp division between monumental pale desert and a productive river corridor: palms, irrigation, cultivated ground, blue water and dense settlement along the life-giving channel. Older architecture carries Egyptian-inspired Titan-forged geometry: sandstone, pylons, carved reliefs, broad axial approaches, obelisks and monumental scale. Those surviving physical objects need not share the current faith. Tol’vir-built working spaces have broad entrances, ramps and generous turning room for quadrupedal bodies when that construction remains. Reserve named pyramids and colossal statues for iconic scenes while letting ordinary wall carvings and geometry retain regional character.

regions.label: Silithus
regions.facts: Silithus is a harsh ancient desert of rippled sand, bare stone, immense exposed remains and unsettling insect-built physical features wherever the hives persist. Pale sand can be washed by strong orange light, with purple-brown rock and strange crystalline materials creating an alien contrast. Regional camps need shade, protected stores and observation. Historic elven stone and insect structures are physical layers independent of present occupants. Do not add Sargeras’s sword, Azerite mining, a mandatory current war or existing canonical druid administration to ordinary scenes. Changed ecology and hive activity must follow the actual timeline.

regions.label: Tanaris
regions.facts: Tanaris is broad bright desert: pale gold and nearly white dunes, vast empty visibility, bare rocky margins and occasional enormous sun-bleached remains. Its eastern blue-water coast contrasts with the glaring interior. Existing commercial settlements favor compact defended yards, wells or stored water, shade and imports; goblin devices and aggressive mercantile clutter apply when supported by builders and technology. Sand-troll stone ruins are persistent site features where mapped. Leave Gadgetzan, Zul’Farrak and the Caverns of Time for iconic scenes. The Cataclysm shoreline change is conditional, not universal.

regions.label: Un'Goro Crater
regions.facts: Un’Goro is exuberantly primeval rather than a conventional settled forest: giant leaves and flowers, looping mossed trunks, hanging vines, saturated green haze, dinosaur-scale passages, strange bright crystals and volcanic ground in its central uplands. Ordinary scenes are small human-scale or other inhabitant-scale footholds in overwhelming ecology. Camps, specimen work, guides and careful routes make travel possible. Keep dinosaur presence optional to an encounter, not a guaranteed attack. Crystal pylons and the central volcano’s exact landmark are reserved for the later iconic pass; local crystals and geothermal margins remain general regional features.

regions.label: Azuremyst Isle
regions.facts: Mist-softened northern island woods, deep blue conifers, moss-green earth, clear streams, rocky shores and pale lavender atmospheric light. Older elven stonework and native woodland settlements can predate the draenei. Exodar fragments and draenei repair settlements require the crash or corresponding local presence.

regions.label: Silvergale / Bloodmyst Isle
regions.facts: Northern misty conifer island, grey stone, wooded ridges, shallow waterways and ancient elven ruins. Before the Exodar’s damage use natural cool woodland tones. After contamination, red crystals, crimson water, reddish earth and altered vegetation provide a striking physical corruption state that persists independently of religion.

regions.label: Feralas Isles
regions.facts: Western rainforest islands: thick moss-green growth, drooping old trees, humid green sea haze, dark coastal rock, warm sand and older kaldorei works. Sardor and Seething Shore share natural coast assets; Feathermoon’s destruction, naga occupation and Azerite exposures are local state.

regions.label: Borean Tundra
regions.facts: A wide, exposed frontier of tawny tundra and glacial flats, with rocky coasts, sparse scrub, mammoth country and localized steaming mineral fields. Keep the horizon broad. Coast life emphasizes fishing and stored provisions; inland travel emphasizes distance and shelter. Existing settlements take the current local cultural skin rather than permanently belonging to Wrath-era expedition factions.

regions.label: Sholazar Basin
regions.facts: A miraculous lush basin surrounded by frozen Northrend: dense warm jungle, broad leaves, abundant water, pale rock shelves, steam and surviving titan environmental works. Hunt camps, river settlements and guardian installations are site-dependent. The green climate assumes functioning regional protection; breached or ruined protection gets a separately selected damaged variant rather than compulsory Wrath-era invasion.

regions.label: Icecrown Glacier
regions.facts: An immense dark glacier: blue-black ice, exposed rock, serrated frozen ravines, cold cyan light and vast logistical distances. In occupied Scourge areas, saronite bastions, corpse stores and necromantic industry add the region’s dreadful engineered character. Base travel remains frozen terrain. Active soul machinery, slaves, undead troops, war-front camps and victory monuments require current state; the geography does not predetermine the campaign.

regions.label: Isle of Conquest
regions.facts: A northern maritime resource island: rocky coasts, cold blue water, exposed ridges and valuable harbours. Its many ordinary sites can host quarrying, industrial storage and fortified logistics when actually built. Horde-versus-Alliance permanent battleground status, airships, oil refineries and siege factories are state-dependent overlays; geological and coastal character works under changing rulers and cultures.

regions.label: Dragonblight
regions.facts: A vast, wind-scoured arctic basin where immense ancient dragon bones interrupt pale snow and ruined roads. Civilization feels small against draconic age and bodily scale. Sheltered coasts and settlements provide warmth. Shrine ecosystems, active necromancy and living dragons belong to verified subsite or state variants; the cold land and naturally ancient remains do not imply current Scourge control.

regions.label: Storm Peaks
regions.facts: Severe vertical mountains where frozen ridges, sheer drops and violent wind frame titan engineering on colossal scales. Ordinary habitation must show wind shelter, steep approaches and stored fuel. Vrykul, frost dwarves, giants, taunka and constructs supply separate current cultural or bodily versions. Ancient titan masonry may remain after political and religious change; live mechanisms and corruption are independently selected states.

regions.label: Crystalsong Forest
regions.facts: A magically transformed forest of luminous white-violet crystal trees, purple ground and surviving ancient elven stonework. Its glassy brilliance and mineral delicacy remain physical regional character regardless of present culture or faith. Ruins, spirit manifestations and functioning arcane studies vary by site and state. Dalaran’s presence is timeline-dependent and excluded from these generic assets.

regions.label: Grizzly Hills
regions.facts: Warm amber conifer wilderness: immense red-brown trunks, moss, fast rivers, wooded ravines, rocky hills, working timber and deep woodland shelter. Furbolg clan craft, human trapper lodges, vrykul remains and industrial logging are independently selected layers. The forest can support both abundance and isolation; current owners and operations determine which inhabited variant exists.

regions.label: Howling Fjord
regions.facts: A maritime northern realm of sheer fjord walls, evergreen forests, wind-cut uplands, rocky islands and autumn-coloured grass. Vrykul timber-and-stone grandeur is a surviving local architectural layer, not a permanent claim about current residents. Travel alternates between exposed heights and constrained sea landings, with steep approaches and unusually large older structures.

regions.label: Wintergrasp
regions.facts: A high frozen valley with snowfields, cold lakes, rocky ridges and surviving titan stonework. Element-rich terrain offers a rationale for extraction and work sites. Regular shores and routes remain available beyond fortifications. Workshops, siege engines and permanent battlefront behavior require the current built and military state, not the zone’s WoW PvP identity.

regions.label: Zul'Drak
regions.facts: A terraced ice-troll civilization organized into rising stone precincts: huge stairs, elevated routes, severe carved animal faces, fortified enclosures and frostbitten woods. Northern elevations are colder and whiter; lower terraces admit darker soil and trees. Treat Drakkari monumentality as existing regional heritage. Living loa cult, desperate god-slaughter, Scourge ruin and current ownership require their actual present state.

regions.label: Strand of the Ancients
regions.facts: A warmer southern island strand where sand, coarse grass, palms and weathered boulders surround ancient titan-built walls, fluted columns and gold-trimmed stone. General approaches and repurposed minor enclosures are reusable without reproducing the iconic relic chamber. scenes.label: Highmountain: Pine Valley Woodland
scenes.art: Highmountain lower-valley woodland of tall narrow firs and pines beneath enormous pale-grey mountain walls. Thick green grass, moss, exposed roots, and scattered heavy boulders cover the sheltered ground; a glimpse of blue-white alpine water appears through the deeper trees. The trunks retain their own impressive scale while the stone columns behind dwarf the entire forest. Fresh cool daylight catches the canopy, leaving blue-green shade close to the floor. Compose a natural level pocket beside a boulder and several overlapping wooded slopes, expressing sheltered abundance within a monumentally vertical landscape.
scenes.facts: Pine resin and damp moss scent the sheltered valley. Roots cross the thick grass between heavy pale boulders, and the mountain walls rise far above the tree crowns. Water sounds reach the woodland through its deeper green shade. Trunks and sloping ground interrupt the near view, while openings reveal a striking amount of vertical distance. The level pocket beside the boulder offers firm footing and natural cover, with quieter air than the exposed heights overhead.
scenes.purpose: A recurring regional meeting place. Its physical affordances leave individual conduct to the participants.
scenes.review: Authored recurring environment; not a named landmark, guaranteed occupation or campaign event.

scenes.label: Highmountain: Colossal Pale Rock Country
scenes.art: Highmountain rock country rises in immense pale-grey jagged columns, towering cliffs, and deep irregular clefts. Small grass pockets and thin pines cling to broad natural shelves, with snow lingering in shaded upper seams. The foreground is a substantial fractured ledge overlooking successive levels of stone rather than a smooth scenic plateau. Cool blue distance magnifies the height; warm daylight reveals the rock's hard edges and enormous scale. Keep vegetation sparse but real on sheltered ground, making the contrast between tiny living patches and immense vertical geology the scene's central visual grammar.
scenes.facts: Hard pale stone gives the ledge an uneven but solid surface. Thin grass grows in the cracks, and a few pines mark shelves far below the towering columns. The open edge reveals successive depths until blue distance softens their detail. Wind moves sharply across the exposed ground; an inward cleft gives a smaller lee where voices become clearer. Loose fragments gather at the ledge's margins, while shaded upper seams retain visible snow above the living green pockets.
scenes.purpose: A recurring regional meeting place. Its physical affordances leave individual conduct to the participants.
scenes.review: Authored recurring environment; not a named landmark, guaranteed occupation or campaign event.

scenes.label: Highmountain: High Alpine Snowfields
scenes.art: Highmountain alpine snowfields stretch between immense jagged grey ridges and sheer pale stone columns. Blue shadow fills the snow's deeper folds, while exposed dark rock and thin ice interrupt wind-scoured shoulders. Small hardy growth survives only at the lowest sheltered cracks. Frame a broad snow shelf beside a massive natural rock recess, with successive peaks rising beyond a cold luminous sky. The terrain should feel tall, hard, and powerfully vertical, with legible crust and drift textures and enough scale to distinguish these heights from the greener inhabited valleys below.
scenes.facts: Cold light catches the snow crust between jagged grey ridges. Loose powder gathers in deep folds, while exposed stone gives darker, harder footing along the shoulder. The open height offers a vast view interrupted by the nearest columns. Wind carries sound away across the shelf. Within the broad rock recess, the air is quieter and nearby voices recover their clarity, though thin shaded ice makes the ground slick close to the stone wall.
scenes.purpose: A recurring regional meeting place. Its physical affordances leave individual conduct to the participants.
scenes.review: Authored recurring environment; not a named landmark, guaranteed occupation or campaign event.

scenes.label: Highmountain: Deep Mineral Caverns
scenes.art: A vast natural Highmountain cavern with immense uneven stone columns, broad rock shelves, and deep openings extending beyond the foreground. Mineral seams and crystalline pockets catch cool faint light; patches of large wild fungi gather around damp cracks near small pools. The rock's brown-grey warmth contrasts with blue-green glints, making the underworld feel earthy and inhabitable rather than empty black space. Compose a substantial natural shelf with a sheltered recess beside it, preserving depth, darkness, and an open view into adjoining clefts. No furniture, carved hall, cultivation bed, or named lair defines the cave.
scenes.facts: Damp mineral air hangs among the immense stone forms. Small pools and wild fungi gather in cracks, while crystalline seams catch faint cool light across the nearer shelves. The cavern extends beyond the visible columns into deeper darkness. Firm rock offers clear footing where the ledge is dry; moisture makes its lower edge slick. Drips return as layered echoes, and voices travel farther than expected through the open clefts before softening in the sheltered recess beside the shelf.
scenes.purpose: A recurring regional meeting place. Its physical affordances leave individual conduct to the participants.
scenes.review: Authored recurring environment; not a named landmark, guaranteed occupation or campaign event.

scenes.label: Stormheim: Golden Birch Woodland
scenes.art: Stormheim woodland glows with dense golden birch crowns and white-barked trunks among tall dark firs. Ochre leaf litter and green grass cover a gently uneven floor, broken by grey boulders and exposed roots. Immense rugged cliff walls rise beyond the forest, but warm clear daylight gives the foreground an unexpectedly luminous northern beauty. Compose a natural open patch between overlapping tree clusters, with deeper evergreen shade at its edge. Strong gold, dark green, pale bark, and weighty grey stone should establish the region without halls, carved markers, route furniture, or a named magical tree.
scenes.facts: Golden leaves brighten the woodland floor, and fir resin scents its darker edge. White trunks divide the view into overlapping spaces beneath the warm canopy. Roots and boulders interrupt otherwise steady grassy ground. The cliffs remain visible above the tree crowns, lending the enclosed grove an immense outer frame. Leaf rustle softens nearby voices; deeper fir shade offers greater concealment, while the natural opening gives a clear view of movement between the brighter birches.
scenes.purpose: A recurring regional meeting place. Its physical affordances leave individual conduct to the participants.
scenes.review: Authored recurring environment; not a named landmark, guaranteed occupation or campaign event.

scenes.label: Stormheim: Green Cliff Uplands
scenes.art: Stormheim uplands combine enormous harsh grey cliffs with surprisingly verdant natural shelves. Thick green grass fills hollows between rough outcrops; dark firs and isolated golden birches cling where the stone holds enough soil. Successive ridges step sharply toward the lower country, with blue-grey distance and a wide northern sky emphasizing their relief. Give the foreground a broad grassy shelf beside fractured rock and a deeper sheltered fold. The contrast of hard cliff faces and living green seams should dominate, retaining bright daylight and weathered northern texture without towers or a constructed ascent.
scenes.facts: Green grass thickens where the rugged stone folds inward, while the exposed cliff edges remain bare and hard. The shelf gives a long view into the lower country, then loses it behind the next ridge. Loose fragments gather beside firmer rock. Wind is strong across the open height, carrying voices beyond the shallow cover. A deeper grassy fold and a dark fir cluster create a quieter lee, with the enormous cliffs still visible above their small sheltered space.
scenes.purpose: A recurring regional meeting place. Its physical affordances leave individual conduct to the participants.
scenes.review: Authored recurring environment; not a named landmark, guaranteed occupation or campaign event.

scenes.label: Suramar: Crimson and Violet Woodland
scenes.art: Suramar woodland is saturated with immense crimson-crowned trees, violet shrubs, and rich red leaf litter beneath graceful twisting branches. Cool blue-green ground plants and pale rock interrupt the warm foliage, while softer lavender light gathers in the farther forest. A broad natural hollow leaves clear foreground ground between substantial roots. The crowns are dramatically full and the color almost jewel-like, conveying the countryside's unusual magical-world richness through living growth alone. Layer overlapping tree clusters and shaded inward pockets, with a brighter distant opening and no city tower, estate, or cultivated receiving space.
scenes.facts: Crimson leaves spread across the hollow, and rich foliage scents the cool shade. Substantial roots divide the clear ground from thicker violet growth. Near views end at overlapping crowns and shrubs; a brighter opening reveals more distant lavender air. Leaves soften the sound underfoot and keep conversation close beneath the branches. The inward root pockets give natural cover, while the small open hollow leaves movement easier to notice before it enters the deeper red woodland.
scenes.purpose: A recurring regional meeting place. Its physical affordances leave individual conduct to the participants.
scenes.review: Authored recurring environment; not a named landmark, guaranteed occupation or campaign event.

scenes.label: Suramar: Starlight Rose Country
scenes.art: Open Suramar country rolls beneath richly colored red and violet tree crowns, with thick grass and scattered pale-violet starlight roses giving the foreground delicate jewel-like accents. Low pale stones and softly rounded earthen folds form natural boundaries between brighter meadow and deeper woodland shade. Cool luminous dusk or soft blue daylight preserves the unusual floral color, with a lavender distance beyond the nearest rise. The scene should remain broad ordinary countryside, emphasizing graceful growth, intricate small flowers, and sheltered grassy hollows rather than vineyards, gardens, buildings, or obvious arcane machinery.
scenes.facts: Delicate pale-violet flowers rise from the thick grass beside low stones. Red tree crowns cast separate pockets of shade across the rolling ground. The open meadow offers a clear view to the next rise, while its shallow folds hide the nearest low spaces. Soft turf gives steady footing outside the denser plants. A mild floral scent hangs close to the ground, and the woodland edge provides a more screened pause without losing sight of the bright flower country.
scenes.purpose: A recurring regional meeting place. Its physical affordances leave individual conduct to the participants.
scenes.review: Authored recurring environment; not a named landmark, guaranteed occupation or campaign event.

scenes.label: Suramar: Pale Canyon Waterbanks
scenes.art: A Suramar freshwater margin deep within pale rocky canyon walls, where clear blue water and a white cascade reflect cool light onto curved natural stone. Crimson and violet foliage grows along high ledges and lower roots, with vines trailing toward mossy banks. The foreground includes a dry shelf beside legible shallows, while deeper blue water continues between immense enclosing cliffs. Use soft lavender distance, jewel-like plants, and hard pale geology to preserve the region's refined natural palette. Compose shelter beneath an inward rock fold and an open view along the water, without arches, bridges, or towers.
scenes.facts: Cool water reflects onto the pale canyon wall, and the cascade's steady sound fills the narrower bank. Vines and red-violet roots screen the edge where moss reaches the shallows. The dry shelf gives firmer ground above wet smooth stone. Sight extends along the water before the canyon's curve hides its deeper course. Voices soften near the cascade and become clearer beneath the inward fold, where the surrounding rock creates a small sheltered space within the immense gorge.
scenes.purpose: A recurring regional meeting place. Its physical affordances leave individual conduct to the participants.
scenes.review: Authored recurring environment; not a named landmark, guaranteed occupation or campaign event.

scenes.label: Val’sharah: Ancient Living Forest
scenes.art: Ancient Val'sharah forest rises in colossal living trunks and immense twisting roots above saturated green ground. Ferns, flowering vines, pale blossoms, and softly luminous blue-green plants crowd the shaded floor, while the canopy folds into deep violet-blue distance. Broad roots arch naturally over pockets of firmer soil, creating intimate enclosures inside a landscape of overwhelming living scale. White sunlight catches only the highest leaves and small openings near the foreground. Let the trees feel graceful, exuberant, and almost dreamlike through their organic forms, with no grown house, bridge, shrine, or named world tree.
scenes.facts: Wet bark and flowers scent the deep green shade. Immense roots divide the ground into small enclosed pockets, with ferns and blue-green plants thickening along their edges. A few openings reveal the canopy's extraordinary height. Firm soil lies between the roots, though soft growth conceals its smaller irregularities. Leaf drips and distant water soften close voices. The forest offers abundant natural cover, while each bright gap briefly exposes the movement passing between its enormous living forms.
scenes.purpose: A recurring regional meeting place. Its physical affordances leave individual conduct to the participants.
scenes.review: Authored recurring environment; not a named landmark, guaranteed occupation or campaign event.

scenes.label: Dun Morogh: Sheltered rocky foothills
scenes.art: An unnamed sheltered foothill stopping ground in Warcraft's Dun Morogh. A clear firm shelf of weathered grey mountain stone is enclosed by dense stout conifers, thick roots and spare low alpine plants. Towering cold-coloured mountain silhouettes rise behind the forest. The immediate stopping ground is bare rock and needle litter, without snowdrifts, active precipitation or a forced seasonal event. Keep a spacious open foreground and cool diffuse light; no building or famous landmark.
scenes.facts: A sheltered rocky shelf opens between thick conifer roots and spare low mountain plants. Cold-coloured ridges rise beyond the forest, while rough stones and needle litter divide the nearer approaches. The clear firm ground offers a place to pause away from the exposed heights; its recesses permit a quieter exchange.
scenes.purpose: A regional mountain stopping place that does not require a snow-cover observation.
scenes.review: Original conservative regional variation; visible snowfields remain independently winter-gated.

scenes.label: Military camp reception awning
scenes.art: Inside a broad temporary Warcraft army reception awning. Thick weathered tan canvas closes the back and side walls around heavy portable timber supports. A large unlettered map table, plain folding benches, rolled blankets, modest cord-bound storage and unmarked shields occupy the edges. A very wide clear level central strip allows differently sized visitors to approach the receiving table. The canvas masks the exterior, leaving the biome, weather and wider army unspecified. Restrained amber lamplight on tactile canvas, warm timber and neutral brown-grey firm ground. No soldiers, bodies, blood, faction heraldry, flags, weapon display, battle, captive, triumphal spoils, landscape vista or readable map marks.
scenes.facts: Heavy canvas walls enclose a broad receiving space around a portable timber table. Plain benches, cord-bound stores and rolled blankets stand clear of the central approach. The side screens permit a quieter exchange beside the larger table, while warm lamplight reaches the canvas and worn wooden fittings. The enclosed view gives little indication of the wider camp.
scenes.purpose: A temporary reception space associated with observed local military presence. Actual allegiance, welcome, guards, conflict and present activity come from the encounter.
scenes.review: Local province army presence, never a general war flag. Portable ordinary camp affordances are authored convention, not a claim of a named army, friendly occupation or ongoing battle.
